rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords in Oakland cannot ask about, consider, or use an applicant's or tenant's criminal history to deny housing, terminate tenancy, charge higher deposits/rent, refuse family members, or disqualify from rental assistance programs, with limited exceptions (e.g., lifetime sex offender registry checks under specific procedures, and public housing federal requirements).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental housing, buildings, or units in the City of Oakland, except single-family dwellings where the owner occupies the dwelling as a principal residence.
rules.exemptions: Single-family dwellings where the owner occupies the dwelling as his or her principal residence; lifetime sex offender registry checks under specified conditions; public housing providers subject to federal eligibility requirements.
rules.penalty: Violations may be subject to an administrative citation.
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of this Article is to limit the use of criminal history in tenant selection policies in order to give previously incarcerated persons or other persons with a criminal history a fair opportunity to compete for rental housing

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is a single-family dwelling occupied by the owner as a principal residence, or is public housing subject to federal eligibility requirements
